text: Government adopts plan to manage trade balance, curb risks

HÀ NỘI - The Vietnamese Government has approved a plan to manage trade balance and prevent risks in international trade through 2030, with an aim of promoting sustainable exports, diversifying supply chains and guarding against unfair trade practices.

Issued under Resolution 403/NQ-CP on November 21, the plan introduces measures to address trade imbalances, prevent illegal transshipment and origin fraud and strengthen controls on goods produced using forced labour.

The plan seeks to balance export expansion with imports of machinery, equipment, materials and technology needed for domestic production, while improving the quality and domestic added value of Vietnamese exports.
It also aims to reduce dependence on a small number of export markets, products and imported input suppliers, while strengthening supply chain resilience and ensuring fair trade.

The Government will establish early warning mechanisms to identify potential risks, including trade barriers, illegal transshipment, origin fraud, excess production capacity and excessive reliance on imported inputs.
To improve trade surplus management and prevent international trade risks, the focus will be on improving regulations on trade management, rules of origin and the prevention of trade circumvention.
In addition, efforts will be stepped up to strengthen data-based monitoring and risk management, diversify supply chains and increase added value.

Under the plan, the Ministry of Industry and Trade will develop databases to monitor the sources of production inputs, particularly in key export industries, and assess their dependence on imported materials while seeking to increase added value and localisation rates.
The State Bank of Vietnam will work with relevant agencies to clarify monetary and credit policies that could face allegations of creating unfair trade advantages or contributing to excess capacity.
Meanwhile, the Ministry of Home Affairs will review labour regulations and develop legal guidelines for import bans on goods produced using forced labour.

The proposed framework will allow authorities to identify high-risk products, regions and suppliers, request businesses to demonstrate the origin of raw materials and production conditions, and suspend customs clearance where there are sufficient grounds for concern.
The trade ministry will encourage businesses to strengthen supply chain traceability and verify the origin of imported materials to avoid sourcing from facilities suspected of using forced labour.

In conjunction with other relevant ministries and agencies, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs will work to strengthen dialogue with trading partners and communicate Việt Nam's efforts to promote balanced and sustainable trade.
Customs statistics show that as of November 15, Việt Nam ran a trade deficit of US$11.74 billion.
MB Securities estimates that an increase in exports through December will narrow this gap to $8-10 billion for the full year. - BIZHUB/VNS
